waypoints.name: Marble Mountain Sno-Park
waypoints.note: Standard winter/spring trailhead; climbing permit required above 4,800 ft year-round.
waypoints.directions: From I-5 Exit 21 at Woodland, follow SR 503 east about 30 miles to Cougar. Continue east on Lewis River Road, which becomes Forest Road 90, to the Forest Road 83 junction, go left and continue roughly 6 mi to where the road ends at the Marble Mountain Sno-Park, where the road is gated in winter and spring. A Washington Sno-Park permit is required December through March, and a Mount St. Helens climbing permit is required above 4,800 ft year-round.

waypoints.name: Mount St. Helens Summit
waypoints.note: Breaks treeline near 3,700 ft at Chocolate Falls, joins the Monitor Ridge route near 7,400 ft, then follows the crater rim west to the true high point.
waypoints.directions: Follow the Swift Creek Trail #244 north through forest about 2 miles to treeline near Chocolate Falls (about 3,700 ft) and just above the falls, get across Swift Creek to its west bank. Follow posts, then cairns and wands, up the Worm Flows onto Worm Flow Ridge past the old seismic station near 6,200 ft, join the Monitor Ridge route near 7,400 ft, climb about 850 ft more to the crater rim and walk a quarter mile west along it to the high point.

waypoints.name: Schriebers Meadow / Park Butte Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From WA-20 at milepost 82, turn north onto Baker Lake Road (FS Road 11) and drive 12.5 miles to just past the Rocky Creek bridge. Turn left on FS Road 12 for 3.6 miles, then stay right on FS Road 13 for 5.3 miles to its end at the Schriebers Meadow (Park Butte) trailhead, about 3,360 ft. Road 13 is potholed and rocky; high clearance helps. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

waypoints.name: Crag View Camp
waypoints.directions: Take the Scott Paul Trail, which branches off within about a hundred feet of the trailhead. Around 4,600 ft, shortly after the first open meadow with views of Baker and Shuksan, leave the maintained trail at an unmarked junction for the climbers' path that climbs north up the ridge to Crag View, about 6,500 ft. The last hundred feet or so narrow to an exposed class 3 scramble.

waypoints.name: Mount Baker Summit
waypoints.directions: Rope up and head north up the Squak Glacier, west of the rock Prow, toward Sherman Peak. Near 9,600 ft traverse northwest to the Sherman Crater rim and join the Easton route, then climb the Roman Wall, about 1,000 ft of 35-40 degree snow, and cross the summit plateau north to Grant Peak.

waypoints.name: Boulder Ridge Trailhead
waypoints.note: Boulder Ridge Trail #605 off Baker Lake Rd/FS 1130/1131.
waypoints.directions: From Sedro-Woolley, drive SR 20 east about 16 miles to milepost 82 and turn north on Baker Lake Road (FS 11). Continue about 18 miles; just past Boulder Creek Campground and the Boulder Creek bridge, turn left on FS 1130 for about 1 mile, then left on FS 1131 to the road end and the Boulder Ridge Trailhead (Trail #605) at about 2,700 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

waypoints.name: Mt. Baker summit (Grant Peak)
waypoints.directions: Follow Boulder Ridge Trail #605 about 2 nearly flat miles to a boggy clearing at the wilderness boundary, then a steep, unmaintained boot path up heather over a Class 3 rock band near 4,700 ft. Stay on the moraine crest north of Boulder Creek to camp where the ridge meets the ice, then rope up and climb the glacier west, south of the cleaver; skirt the big buttress near 9,500 ft to the south, cross the bergschrund and finish up steep snow to Grant Peak.

waypoints.name: North Fork Sauk River Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Darrington, drive the Mountain Loop Highway south about 16 miles to Forest Road 49 (Sloan Creek Road), turn east and drive about 6.4 miles to the North Fork Sauk Trailhead parking lot at about 2,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and a free Glacier Peak Wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

waypoints.name: Kennedy Ridge high camp
waypoints.note: Standard high camp on snow and pumice on the Kennedy Ridge shoulder. Snowmelt water only, and pumice holds stakes poorly; open to weather in every direction.
waypoints.directions: Hike the North Fork Sauk trail to the PCT near White Pass and follow the PCT north to Glacier Ridge. About 0.7 mile past the Glacier Creek crossing an unmarked climbers' path leaves the trail and climbs snow and pumice to the camp near 7,200 ft.

waypoints.name: Glacier Peak Summit
waypoints.directions: Gain the Kennedy Glacier, a crumbling mess of moraine and big boulders at its toe, and climb it roped to the 8,800 ft saddle where Frostbite Ridge begins. Follow the crest over pumice and 45-50 degree snow to the Rabbit Ears, pass through their notch and downclimb about 150 ft of class 3, then climb one to two pitches of alpine ice to the crater rim. Cross the crater and climb its far wall to the summit.

waypoints.name: Killen Creek Trailhead (Trail #113, FR-2329)
waypoints.note: Standard start, via High Camp and a traverse east past Lava Ridge. Muddy Meadows trailhead, farther east, is an alternative start for the Lava and Lyman glaciers.
waypoints.directions: From Randle on US 12, take Forest Road 23 south about 32 miles, the last stretch gravel, to FR 2329, then turn east past Takhlakh Lake about 5 miles to the trailhead. From Trout Lake, take Mt Adams Road and FR 23 north about 24 miles to the same junction. Roads are seasonal. A free wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead; a Mt. Adams climbing pass is needed above 7,000 ft May through September.

waypoints.name: Mount Adams summit
waypoints.directions: Follow Killen Creek Trail #113 about 3.1 miles to the PCT at about 6,100 ft and continue straight across on High Camp Trail #10 a mile to High Camp. Traverse east and southeast off-trail across the lava fields, the toe of the Lava Glacier, and around or over the toe of Lava Ridge to the base of the Lyman Glacier near 8,000 ft. Climb either lobe of the glacier to the crux chute near 10,000 ft, then easier snow to the summit plateau and summit.
